questions.question: You have 3 nickels. How many cents is that?
questions.explain: Each nickel is worth 5 cents, so you skip-count by 5s: 5, 10, 15. The trap is just counting the 3 coins instead of adding their value.

questions.question: You have 4 dimes. How many cents is that?
questions.explain: Each dime is worth 10 cents, so you skip-count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. Watch out for counting just the 4 dimes or mixing up a dime with a nickel.

questions.question: You have 5 toonies. How many dollars is that?
questions.explain: Each toonie is worth 2 dollars, so you skip-count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Don't just say the number of coins, and don't mix up a toonie with a nickel.

questions.question: You have 4 nickels. How many cents is that?
questions.explain: Each nickel is 5 cents, so you skip-count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. A common slip is using the wrong step, like adding 2 each time instead of 5.

questions.question: Mia puts 3 dimes in her piggy bank. How many cents does she have?
questions.explain: Each dime is 10 cents, so you count by 10s: 10, 20, 30. Be careful not to just count the 3 dimes or add the wrong amount each time.

questions.question: Dad gives Ben 4 toonies for his birthday. How many dollars is that?
questions.explain: Each toonie is 2 dollars, so you skip-count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. Don't just say 4 (the number of coins) or mix up a toonie with a nickel.

questions.question: You have 5 nickels and you want to find the total. What number do you add each time?
questions.explain: A nickel is worth 5 cents, so you add 5 each time: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. Adding 1 is just counting coins, and adding 10 is the step for dimes.

questions.question: You have 4 nickels. Your friend gives you 1 more. Now you skip-count all your nickels by 5s. What number do you say last?
questions.explain: Now you have 5 nickels, so you count: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. The last number is 25. Watch out for counting just the 5 coins or using the wrong step.

questions.question: Jake has 4 nickels. He says, 'I have 4 cents.' What did he do wrong?
options: He counted coins, not their value.
He thought a nickel is 2 cents.
He added 2 each time instead of 5.
He counted one nickel too many.
questions.explain: Jake counted 4 coins and called that 4 cents. He should have skip-counted by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, to get 20 cents.

questions.question: You have 2 dimes. A friend gives you 3 more dimes. You skip-count all your dimes by 10s. What is your total in cents?
questions.explain: 2 plus 3 is 5 dimes, so you count: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Don't just say 5 (the coins) or think each dime is only 5 cents.

questions.question: Mateo finds 6 nickels in the couch. How many cents is that?
questions.explain: A nickel is 5 cents, so skip-count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Saying 6 only tells how many coins, not how many cents.

questions.question: Ella shakes 5 loonies out of her piggy bank. How many dollars is that?
questions.explain: Each loonie is 1 dollar, so count by 1s: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. A loonie is not 2 dollars, so the total is not 10.

questions.question: Ravi needs 6 dollars for a book. Which set of coins is worth 6 dollars?
questions.explain: Count toonies by 2s: 2, 4, 6. Three toonies make 6 dollars, while 6 toonies would be 12 dollars.

questions.question: Ari has 6 dimes. He wants to know how many cents. Which way is right?
questions.explain: A dime is 10 cents, so count by tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. Counting by ones only counts the coins, not the cents.

questions.question: Noor has only dimes in her hand. She counts 50 cents in all. How many dimes does she have?
questions.explain: Count by 10s until you get to 50: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. That is 5 dimes, because each dime is 10 cents, not 5 cents.

questions.question: Kai has 5 toonies. He counts 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. What went wrong?
options: He thinks a toonie is 1 dollar.
questions.explain: Five toonies get five counts: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Kai said one number too many, so his real total is 10 dollars.

questions.question: Priya has 5 nickels. She spends 1 nickel on a gumball. How many cents does she have left?
questions.explain: First take away 1 nickel, so 4 nickels are left. Then count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20 cents.

questions.question: Leo has 4 toonies. His aunt gives him 2 more toonies. How many dollars now?
questions.explain: Leo now has 6 toonies, so count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. Do not stop at 8, because the 2 new toonies count too.
